diagnosis.summary: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the 10:15 deployment, breaching the SLO. The issue is likely due to the new database connection pool configuration in the deployment.
diagnosis.root_cause: The checkout-api deployment reduced the database connection pool size to 10 connections, leading to connection exhaustion and increased latency.

evidence.finding: Production p95 latency is 2150 ms, breaching the SLO of 400 ms.
Staging p95 latency is 180 ms with the same version, indicating the issue is environment-specific.
The commit a91f3c2 removed database pool settings and set max_connections to 10, which is likely the cause of the connection exhaustion.
Production database connection pool is fully utilized (in_use: 10, max_connections: 10) with 143 waiting connections.
Production database acquire_wait_p95_ms is 1800 ms, indicating long waits for connections.
All checkout-api pods in production are running version v4.17, confirming the deployment is active.
The deployment DEP-88213 was triggered by the release pipeline and completed successfully.

ruled_out: The staging environment with the same version does not show the issue, ruling out a general code bug.
The deployment was successful and did not fail, ruling out a deployment failure as the cause.

proposal.rationale: The Checkout API's p95 latency has increased to 2150 ms in production after the deployment of version v4.17, breaching the SLO. The root cause is likely the reduced database connection pool size to 10 connections, leading to connection exhaustion and increased latency. Rolling back to the previous version, v4.16, is the safest remediation to restore service to the expected performance levels.
